pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: The combination of acute psychiatric breakdown progressing to orofacial dyskinesias, extreme delta brush pattern on EEG, and the detection of an unsuspected ovarian teratoma in a young female. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural tissue contained within the ovarian teratoma expresses NMDA (N-methyl-D-aspartate) receptors, inciting an autoimmune response. Autoantibodies targeted against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor cross the blood-brain barrier and cause selective cross-linking and internalization of synaptic NMDA receptors, predominantly within forebrain and hippocampal regions. This down-regulation disrupts GABAergic inhibitory pathways, leading to uninhibited glutamate release, psychosis, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, and central respiratory failure.
